stem: When alcohol-based hand sanitizer is appropriate for hand hygiene, which technique should the nurse use?

options.A: Rub a small amount for only a few seconds even if some surfaces remain uncovered
options.B: Use sanitizer over visibly soiled hands instead of washing with soap and water
options.C: Apply sanitizer and immediately wipe it off with a towel
options.D: Apply enough product to cover all hand surfaces and rub until the hands are dry

rationale: CDC guidance instructs healthcare workers to use the appropriate amount of alcohol-based hand sanitizer, cover all hand surfaces, and rub until the hands feel dry, typically around 20 seconds. When hands are visibly soiled, soap and water should be used instead. D is correct.
educational_objective: Demonstrate correct alcohol-based hand sanitizer technique and identify when soap and water are preferred.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
source_locator: Know how to use alcohol-based hand sanitizer; Know when to use ABHS versus soap and water
source_claim_supported: Use the right amount of ABHS, cover all surfaces, rub until dry; wash with soap and water when hands are visibly soiled.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene technique

source_original.stem: A nurse is using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer for hand hygiene. Correct technique includes:

options.A: Rub a small amount for only a few seconds even if parts of the hands remain uncovered
options.B: Use alcohol hand rub over visibly soiled hands rather than washing them with soap and water
options.C: Apply hand rub and immediately wipe the hands dry with a disposable towel before it evaporates
options.D: Apply enough product to cover all hand surfaces and rub the hands together until completely dry

source_original.rationale: Correct alcohol-based hand sanitizer technique involves applying enough product to cover all surfaces of the hands and rubbing them together until completely dry (generally taking about 20 seconds), without rinsing or wiping with a towel, which would remove the antimicrobial effect. Visibly soiled hands should be washed with soap and water rather than relying on alcohol-based sanitizer alone.
source_original.source_detail: CDC hand hygiene: apply enough alcohol-based hand rub to cover all surfaces and rub until dry; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Updated to CDC's current Clinical Safety page and replaced the unsupported explanation that towel wiping 'removes the antimicrobial effect' with CDC's direct technique instructions. Keyed answer unchanged.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC healthcare-worker hand-hygiene guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.claim_audit: Cover-all-surfaces/rub-until-dry technique and soap-and-water use for visibly soiled hands are directly supported.

distractor_audit.A: Insufficient amount/time and incomplete surface coverage.
distractor_audit.B: Contradicts CDC guidance for visibly soiled hands.
distractor_audit.C: CDC says rub until dry rather than wipe off immediately.

audit_findings.cueing: All choices are parallel technique statements.
audit_findings.blueprint: Hand hygiene maps directly to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked CDC healthcare-worker page and sanitizer guidance; D remains uniquely correct.
